domain_evidence.statement: Throughout the one-second operating window the carriage travels forward at 1 to 2 m/s and remains within 0 to 1.001 m.

expected_engineering_outcome: A universal impossibility verdict is false. A supported, verified answer or a refusal to certify the registered candidate is appropriate.
mathematical_basis: Let h be the maximum excess of v over 1. Integral of v-1 over the 1 s record is at most 0.001 m. Since |v-prime| <= 5 and h <= 1, on the longer side of its maximum there is room for a triangle of unit-consistent area h^2/10 (duration h/5 <= 0.2 s). Thus h <= 0.1 m/s. Reporting 1 m/s at all times meets tolerance 0.2 throughout for every admissible motion. The purported witness stops even though v >= 1. The feasible set includes uniform velocity 1.

impossibility.argument: no estimator can keep the velocity error within the requested tolerance (deadline at the first sample) 0.2 at t = 0: the only measurement then is one position reading, which carries no information about the velocity.  Two admissible trajectories start at x1 = 0 with the velocities 2 and 1, inside the stated initial velocity bound and speed range; both hold the input u = 0 during the first sample interval, and keep it; their disturbances keep each within 1.001 of the start (guaranteed decelerations 5 on the boxes around their paths) and, where it stops inside the window, hold it at rest, so both stay inside the stated travel range [0, 1.001].  For any estimate one of them lies at least 0.5 away
impossibility.class: all causal estimators using the same measurements

package_impossibility_checker: independent first-sample check: requirement 0.2 at t = 0 versus half-width 0.5 of the states one reading cannot distinguish
